title: Preparation of feed with metal oxide nanoparticles for nanomaterial dietary exposure to fish and use in OECD TG 305
author: Bermejo-Nogales, Rucandio, et al.

steps.title: Prepare NP‑oil suspension
steps.instruction: Create a homogeneous nanoparticle‑oil dispersion for spiking the feed.

substeps.instruction: Combine 60 mg of the selected nanomaterial powder (CeO₂: 5–10 nm, 99.72 % purity, 85–170 m²/g; TiO₂ (NM‑105): 78 % anatase, 14 % rutile, 8 % amorphous, 21 nm, 99.5 % purity, 50 ± 15 m²/g; or ZnO: 20–30 nm, 99.72 % purity) with 3 mL refined sunflower or olive oil (Eroski brand; sunflower oil 0.2 % max acidity, olive oil 0.4 % max acidity) in a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Vortex the mixture at 2500 rpm for 1 min to obtain a uniform suspension (20 mg NP/mL, 2 % w/v).

steps.title: Weigh fish feed pellets
steps.instruction: Measure the amount of feed that will be spiked.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 60 g of 3 mm fish feed pellets and place them in a 250 mL glass beaker.

steps.title: Apply suspension to feed
steps.instruction: Add the NP‑oil suspension to the feed at the correct ratio.

substeps.instruction: Pour the NP‑oil suspension over the feed, using 50 µL of suspension per gram of feed (total ≈3 mL for 60 g).
Note that the suspension is viscous; a small volume will remain in the tube and cannot be avoided.

steps.title: Mix for uniform coverage
steps.instruction: Ensure all pellets are evenly coated with the suspension.

substeps.instruction: Stir the mixture with a glass rod until the pellets are uniformly covered.

steps.title: Dry spiked pellets
steps.instruction: Allow the coated feed to dry before storage.

substeps.instruction: Leave the coated pellets at room temperature (≈20‑25 °C) overnight to dry.

steps.title: Store dried pellets
steps.instruction: Keep the prepared feed under conditions that preserve nanoparticle integrity.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the dried pellets to an airtight, light‑protected container and store at 4 °C for the duration of the bioaccumulation study.

steps.title: Acid‑digest feed samples
steps.instruction: Digest feed for ICP‑OES metal analysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare an acid mixture of nitric acid (HNO₃, 65 % w/w), hydrofluoric acid (HF, 48 % w/w) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂, 30 % w/w) in the proportion 77.7 % : 11.1 % : 11.1 %.
Place the feed sample in a DigiPrep digestion vessel.
Heat to 75 °C and hold for 15 min.
Increase temperature to 115 °C and hold for 60 min.
Cool the digest, dilute as required, and transfer to ICP‑OES sample tubes.

steps.title: Acid‑digest NP‑oil residues
steps.instruction: Digest remaining NP‑oil suspension and residues from labware.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a digestion mixture of 71.4 % HNO₃ (65 % w/w), 14.28 % HF (48 % w/w) and 14.28 % of the NP‑oil suspension (or 1.42 % NP‑oil residues).
Transfer the NP‑oil suspension or residue‑containing glassware to HVT50 vessels.
Digest using rotor 12HVT50 in a Multiwave 60 microwave digestion system (Anton Paar, Spain).

steps.title: Analyze metal content by ICP‑OES
steps.instruction: Measure Ce, Ti and Zn concentrations to assess recovery and homogeneity.

substeps.instruction: Run the digested samples on an Agilent 5100 ICP‑OES instrument (Agilent Technologies Spain, S.L.).
Record concentrations of the original NP‑oil suspension, the spiked feed, and any residues to calculate recovery percentages.

description: Here we describe an easy, cost-effective method to prepare metal oxide nanoparticle (NP) spiked fish feed using an oil dispersion and soaking technique for use in manufactured nanomaterials (MN) bioaccumulation testing using the dietary exposure route. This method was developed to address an essential methodological question that remains unanswered regarding the best way to incorporate MNs into feed. An oil dispersion spiking methodology is normally used to add materials, nutrients or even chemicals to fish feed, however its use for MN spiking has been scarcely explored. Spiking of low soluble chemicals by means of corn or fish oil should be considered according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) test guideline (TG) 305 for testing bioaccumulation in fish (Section 4.2.2.2) and can also serve to adjust the dietary lipid concentration [1]. The protocols presented within this TG and its guidance document No. 264 [2] were developed for studies of dietary exposure with metals and organic chemicals, however additional considerations for MN testing have to be made. Thus, the present work concentrates on the use of oil (sunflower or olive oil) as a dispersant for MNs to allow an appropriate addition to feed pellets while avoiding any loss of MNs to the water when fish are being fed. We have focused on the characterization and appropriateness of the use of oil as a dispersant for MNs, giving enough information to potential users so that they can apply a very straightforward appropriate methodology to allow MNs to be administered to fish through the diet, for instance in the framework of the OECD TG 305 for determining bioaccumulation of MNs in fish. The method developed was applied using CeO2, TiO2 and ZnO NP powders and the concentration of respective metal in the spiked feed was analysed to assess overall recovery and homogeneity of coverage.
